correctness.advice: Run your program on the failing inputs above, especially a match in the last position and an empty array.

syntax.advice: Fix every compiler warning; compile with -Wall -Wextra to see them.

structure.feedback: all functions within limits (cyclomatic <= 8, length <= 40); cppcheck found nothing
structure.advice: Keep each function short and simple, and fix what cppcheck reports.

modularity.feedback: work is split into 2 functions: find_first, main
modularity.advice: Move the search into a helper function, for example int find_first(const int *values, int n, int target), and call it from main.

logical.feedback: 8 of 8 edge cases match the reference
logical.advice: Test an empty array (n = 0), a single number, a match in the last position and repeated values.

complexity.advice: Look at each number once from left to right; sorting first costs more than the search itself.

memory_safety.advice: Never read past the end of the array, free what you allocate, and handle n = 0.

evidence.raw_response: {"score":9,"reasons":["clear variable and function names","helpful comments explain edge cases","consistent indentation and spacing"]}

readability.feedback: 9/10 from openai/gpt-oss-120b: clear variable and function names; helpful comments explain edge cases; consistent indentation and spacing
readability.advice: Use clear names, consistent indentation and a short comment above each function.

originality.advice: Write the solution yourself and be ready to explain every line.

usefulness.use_case: Explaining a wrong answer to the student
usefulness.example: add.c prints -2147483648 for the input 2147483647 1. The report shows the input, the expected 2147483648, what the program printed, and says to use long long.
usefulness.benefit: The student sees exactly which input breaks the program and how to fix it.

usefulness.example: add_copy.c is add_good.c with every name changed. The agent still finds a similarity of 1.00 and raises a flag.
usefulness.benefit: The teacher checks only the flagged pairs instead of every submission.

limitations.limitation: Short programs look copied even when they are not
limitations.example: add.c has a similarity of 1.00 with an answer from the qwen LLM, because the obvious 5-line solution is the same for everyone.
limitations.mitigation: A flag never lowers the grade; the teacher decides.

limitations.limitation: The readability score is the opinion of an LLM
limitations.example: add_syntax_error.c is neatly written but got 3/10 for one missing ';', while the more cramped add.c got 6/10.
limitations.mitigation: Readability is only 10% of the grade, and answers are cached so the score does not change between runs.
